text: This demonstration uses synthetic narration and shows retained project evidence, rather than a live pipeline execution. The collectors handle written feeds, YouTube, and podcasts. Extraction retains substantive text or local transcriptions. Persistent storage identifies records and versions. Only the store component accesses the database. The freshness stage applies an inclusive 30-day UDC publication window.

Publication dates are kept separate from collection dates. The editorial workflow then selects items, creates briefs, writes article and video drafts, and runs checks. Policy and prompts are saved separately from implementation. A human review and approval step comes before the production package. This separation makes stages easier to inspect and rerun, but it also means that a successful mechanical check does not establish factual correctness. Here is one claim traced through the system.

The first article reports India's compound mixed team Olympic quota places, the published paragraph sites World Archery, in the retained article, claim Marker 01C2 connects that passage to the reviewed brief and its source evidence. The source describes a country's quota places. The article therefore distinguishes qualification from an athlete's eventual selection and mixed team competition from an individual compound event. This is a source supported report, followed by a bounded editorial interpretation.

The article also preserves uncertainty. The supplied sources do not fully explain the qualification timing, and two reports disagree about the recurve team final score. The score was omitted rather than choosing one account without resolution. The retained live runs occurred on October 14th and 15th.
